This is the part of the story everybody has heard.
The Aztecs believed that the gods had sacrificed themselves to create the world.
Humans owed them a debt, and the debt was paid in lives.
Stop paying and the universe would end.
So people were sacrificed, most of them prisoners of war.
Two things are worth nolly. First...
The Aztecs did not invent this.
Human sacrifice was practiced across ancient Mexico, by the Maya and by the Aztecs enemies too.
Second, the numbers are disputed.
Sources written after the conquest say that when the Great Temple was rededicated in 1487, 80,400 prisoners died in four days.
Most historians think that figure is inflated and put the real number in the thousands.
